summary.text: A 50-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial flutter, seizure disorder and hypertension presented to the emergency department with altered mental status after her family found her unconscious. She had fever and headaches for the past day and in the ED had fever, tachycardia, leukocytosis and severe fluent aphasia. Neurology did not consider her a thrombolysis candidate and she was admitted for questionable stroke or postictal state.

Head CT and CT angiography were negative and MRI showed left medial temporal hyperintensity. Continuous EEG showed as many as 10 seizures per hour; she received midazolam for seizure suppression and levetiracetam in addition to home lamotrigine. CSF PCR detected Herpes simplex virus 1 with predominant lymphocytosis, and she was upgraded to the ICU for intubation and monitoring of status epilepticus.

Empiric Bactrim, acyclovir, vancomycin and ceftriaxone were started, then all antibiotics were stopped with acyclovir continued. High-sensitivity troponin trended up from 155 to 768 and an echo the same day showed segmental hypokinesis. She was treated with NSTEMI therapy, heparin and a beta-blocker, propafenone was stopped, and amiodarone was started. No coronary angiogram was performed because of resistant seizure activity; vasospasm and plaque rupture could not be excluded.

Repeat echo five days later showed normal LV systolic function with an ejection fraction of 60-65%, and a thallium perfusion scan after recovery from status epilepticus was normal, and the extensive ischemia workup was negative. Stress cardiomyopathy was diagnosed. She became seizure-free after Day 6, midazolam was stopped, and she was extubated, stable for step down and eventually discharged.
